pr_title: Fix hybrid search and unified highlighting
pr_body:
When attempting to use `weight_matches_mode` & unified highlighting, hybrid search with knn throws an error.

This commit addresses this.

closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/101141
pr_comments: Hi @benwtrent, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
This work will take significantly more than this PR. Simply disabling weight based highlighting for now.

comments: well, unwrapping doesn't help. Still trying to find out why we are using a different reader when highlighting vs. building the query.

OK, I think the issue is this:

 - The query is built with a TopLevel directory reader and it utilizes its context
 - Then later, we iterate specific doc-ids, offsets, and a particular subreader when highlighting: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2a44d3f40d7d7cff6c343881f49690a76eafb1a5/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/fetch/FetchPhaseDocsIterator.java#L46

Doing `Weight#matches` against `KnnScoreDocQuery` with a sub-reader instead of the top-level will fail every time from what I can tell.

@jimczi @javanna ^ What do y'all think?
FYI, here is a branch with some tests that SHOULD pass, but don't. https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/compare/main...benwtrent:elasticsearch:bugfix/issue-101141?expand=1
I am gonna open a PR to auto-disable weight_mode highlighting when a knn query is present. I think truly fixing it when kNN is around will take more work

review_comments:
This is frustrating, I am not 100% sure how to fully fix this other than this.

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d411acecbcbd029ebadbfa533a07c70330d454c8/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/fetch/FetchPhase.java#L120

So, for every hit that is within a given reader context, we set the matching docs and that individual sub-reader. This makes up the `HitContext`. This is then passed to the highlighting processor, and used when making the `FieldHighlightContext`:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/28a504d7a1ee520c52a9dcac9cdee2df0deb6e14/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/fetch/subphase/highlight/DefaultHighlighter.java#L55

Eventually, we get down to finding the offsets here in Lucene: https://github.com/apache/lucene/blob/5694e30bccd13d180cd1a813f532aa12c6ab36dc/lucene/highlighter/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/uhighlight/FieldHighlighter.java#L80

The specific offset class being used is this one: https://github.com/apache/lucene/blob/5694e30bccd13d180cd1a813f532aa12c6ab36dc/lucene/highlighter/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/uhighlight/MemoryIndexOffsetStrategy.java#L104C5-L104C5

Since we are using the weight_offsets, we go down this path: https://github.com/apache/lucene/blob/5694e30bccd13d180cd1a813f532aa12c6ab36dc/lucene/highlighter/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/uhighlight/FieldOffsetStrategy.java#L114

There we see the individual leafReader being wrapped and a new searcher being created around that reader.

So, its the SAME leaf reader, but the context we were expecting in kNN is the top level context. 

In this "fix", I:

 - Verify we just have one leaf (which indicates this path of we wrapped the individual leaf reader)
 - Unwrap it to ensure its one we used before
 - pass the test

This will work only if we reuse the underlying index. The unified highlighter will use a memory index for cases where the highlighted fields don't have the offsets index option. I am not sure how we can fix it without disabling the weight matches mode if we detect a `KnnScoreDocQuery` internally?
@jimczi yeah, I don't know how we can fix it either. I did disable weight matches if we detect that query kind: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/101713
From what I can tell, `FilterLeafReader` can have different context ids. This fails as we may be wrapped or not, or the internal thing will be unwrapped and wrapped a different way later :/
